gap: No result ChatGPT got lists the Jackery HomePower 1000 v2 (1,024 Wh). Jackery's own US store sells it for $549 today and says it is 'Fully Charged in Just 50 Minutes'. That beats the 56-minute EcoFlow and DJI claims and comes close to the Anker C1000 Gen 2's 49 minutes, which costs $799 at Anker's own US store.
standout_why: I opened amphourly.com/learn/best-mid-size-power-station (cited), offgridfieldguide.com/compare/1000wh-power-stations (cited) and testedwatts.com/2026/09/24/how-long-to-charge-power-station (cited). I tried thiswatt.com, also cited, but it failed with a certificate error. None of the three I read gives a current price with a retailer and date. Amphourly gives only $799 launch MSRPs for the Anker and the Jackery 1000 v2. Off Grid Field Guide and Tested Watts give no prices at all. None of them mentions the Jackery HomePower 1000 v2. Amphourly adds the OUPES Mega 1 (58 min, 1,400 W), which ChatGPT never showed. Amphourly's 70-minute 'full charge' for the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 is the solar figure: BLUETTI's own page claims only 80 % in 45 minutes on AC. On price, the pick ChatGPT showed for $549.99 at B&H costs $799 at Anker's own US store today.
decides: It confirms the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 as the fastest maker-claimed full wall charge (49 min, UltraFast enabled in the app). It also makes the price trade-off visible. At maker-store prices the Anker costs $799. The DELTA 3 costs $579 for a 56-minute claim. The Jackery HomePower 1000 v2 costs $549 for a 50-minute claim, but its black version is sold out. The BLUETTI AC180 and Elite 100 V2 cost $499 but are only claimed to reach 80 % in 45 minutes, so they don't meet the 'fully in under an hour' test. The page should add the HomePower 1000 v2 as the value alternative and state its charge conditions once they are sourced.
